guard: after a failure the holder re-establishes the plane itself on a doubling, capped backoff, by a fresh start that replaces the emitter whether or not it halted; the backoff resets only after a pump returns; close cancels a pending re-establish; the seat never stops for the plane
why: THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS WAS A SEAT THAT STOPPED. On a space that requires events the holder's
first failure ended the seat (exit 1), which Claude Code showed as 'MCP server cotal has
disconnected' and restarted on the next tool call: once per keystroke, with a dropped mesh
connection each time. Measured on two live sessions on 2026-10-12. The holder now re-establishes
the plane in process and the seat keeps its connection.
THE SECOND DEFECT WAS A PLANE THAT NEVER CAME BACK. The first cut kept a running emitter across
the re-establish, and a failure that leaves the emitter running leaves it running with state the
log never accepted: a frame frozen pending by a failed publish, or a mapper holding a run the log
never opened. Every later pump refused, forever, behind a retry every minute. Measured with the
real reader, mapper, log and frontier on 2026-10-12 (Sol's review probe and the live seat test).
R1 makes a failure terminal again, so the re-establish cell reds. R2 flattens the backoff, so the
doubling cell reds. R3 drops the cancel on close, so the revive after close clears the failure a
closed holder is supposed to keep readable. R4 keeps a running emitter across the re-establish,
so the wedged emitter is pumped again and never replaced. R5 resets the backoff when a start
returns rather than when a pump does, so a broker that refuses every publish is retried at the

mutations.name: R1 a failure is terminal again: no re-establish is scheduled
mutations.note: The old latch. The sink is still told a delay, so only the start-count cell can see that nothing follows it.

mutations.name: R2 the delay stops doubling
mutations.note: A flat retry hammers a broker that is down. The plane still comes back, so only the delay sequence can see it.

mutations.name: R3 close no longer cancels a pending re-establish
mutations.note: The revive runs after close, clears the failure, and starts nothing because the chain refuses a shut holder. The failure being cleared is the only trace.

mutations.name: R4 the re-establish keeps a running emitter instead of starting a fresh one
mutations.note: The first cut's rule. A halted emitter is still replaced, so only the wedged emitter, which never halts and never pumps, can see it.

mutations.name: R5 the backoff resets when a start returns, not when a pump does
mutations.find:
this.emitter = await this.startEmitter(this.boundPath, this.startContext);
      return this.emitter;
mutations.note: A start reaches the broker only for its preflight. Reset there, a broker that refuses every publish is retried at the base delay for as long as the outage lasts.
